content.text: Job IDs are composed as {node_id_hex}-{millis_since_epoch}-{counter}. When two worker nodes finish boot in the same millisecond and both start counters at 0, the first jobs they enqueue can share an identical job_id if node_id assignment also collides during a brief membership flap.

More commonly, node_id is derived from a truncated MAC hash that collides under certain cloud NIC renames, so the millisecond+counter pair alone is not unique. Duplicate primary keys on job_events then cause the second insert to fail and the job to be dropped after the publish ack.

A safer scheme would use a 128-bit random id or include a process start ulid segment that is unique per process lifetime. Current collision window is small but has produced at least three lost jobs in the last 30 days on the EU pool.
